frontier.hypothesis: Requirement (B) is now a one-scalar problem with a named double bind — out2 must reach a priority in (1473, 1702) WHILE its definition stays in block 0 — and the solver suite is the instrument designed for exactly this shape.
frontier.mechanism: tools/ra_solver models GCC 2.7.2's entire allocation stack (global.c / local-alloc / reload) and inverse_compose.py classify converts a register-seat residual into a typed REACHABLE / FORECLOSED verdict with ranked C-lever vectors. The out2 residual is a pure register-seat residual, and s14 has reduced its surrounding chassis to a form where every other seat is already correct, so the solver's goal is now unambiguous.
frontier.next_probe: Run tools/ra_solver/inverse_compose.py classify against the Z0_honest_ifirst chassis (NOT candidate.c — Z0 is the form whose only defect is this one seat) with stptr 5/41, i 8/99, tbl 4/47, stptr2 6/48, pa4 7/95 and a3 4/99 pinned at their measured values, goal = out2 into $s6; then filter its lever vectors against the block-0-definition constraint from E-s14-5, which no previous solver run carried.

frontier.hypothesis: The +2 emission-order gap between alt_fakefree_floor3_s14.c (floor 3, honest) and candidate.c (floor 1, un-annotated F1) is a sched1 tie-break question, not an RA question, and tools/sched_solver can rule it REACHABLE or FORECLOSED — which decides which of the two forms the pipeline should carry as its base.
frontier.mechanism: sched.c's rank_for_schedule falls back to INSN_LUID for ready insns of equal priority, and the three between-block insns (addiu $s1,0x6C; addiu $s2,0x6C; li $s4,18) are mutually independent with no in-block consumers, so their emission order is decided purely by source order — the same source order that sets reg_live_length(i). tools/sched_solver models both scheduler passes order- and clock-exact.
frontier.next_probe: Run tools/sched_solver on the between-loops block of X0_ipos asking whether any dependency-preserving source order emits addiu $s1, addiu $s2, li $s4,18 in target's order while keeping `i = 0x12;` at LUID position 1; if FORECLOSED, the +2 is proven structural and (A) must be satisfied by some other honest lever, so re-open the search for one (e.g. a 6th honest stptr reference at live 41 = 2926).

frontier.hypothesis: Target's source contains a construct whose insns flow counts and which is deleted AFTER flow fixes reg_n_refs — E-s14-2 proves such a construct must exist — and the surviving candidate family is jump2 / cross-jump tail merging, which runs after allocation so its deletions are free.
frontier.mechanism: flow_analysis fixes reg_n_refs at toplev.c:2983; the passes that can delete an insn afterwards are combine (intra-block only — which is why every between-block spelling died in s8), reload's redundant-copy elimination, and jump2 / cross-jump tail merging. The sanctioned duplicated-statement-into-arms family (.claude/rules/duplicated-statement-into-arms.md) is exactly the cross-jump lever, and s2 measured its ref-lift mechanism CONFIRMED, failing only on byte-neutrality because sched1 interleaved the fall-in copy.
frontier.next_probe: Re-run the duplicated-statement-into-arms construction on the CURRENT Z0_honest_ifirst chassis rather than s2's long-dead split model, targeting out2 rather than tbl, and read the .jump2 dump (pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_80041188) to see whether the duplicated tails re-merge — the sandbox score alone cannot distinguish 'not merged' from 'merged but mis-seated', and the two chassis differ by six sessions of structure so the s2 verdict is not chassis-valid.
